
```{r load}
source("R/setup.R")
national <- load_national()
strata   <- load_strata()
check_eda_inputs(national, strata)
periods  <- period_summary(national)
typical  <- typical_season(national)
peaks    <- peaks_per_season(national)
peak_sum <- peak_summary(peaks)
long     <- national_long(national)
bag_th   <- readr::read_csv(file.path(PATH_REFERENCE, "epidemic_thresholds.csv"),
                            comment = "#", show_col_types = FALSE)
reported <- readr::read_csv(file.path(PATH_REFERENCE, "bag_reported_values.csv"),
                            comment = "#", show_col_types = FALSE)
mem_th     <- mem_thresholds(national)
validation <- mem_validation(national, mem_th, bag_th, reported)
boundaries <- boundaries_both_systems(national, mem_th, peaks)

# Colours: systems as in CONTRIBUTING.md; periods in neutral greys (+ line type)
COL_SYSTEM <- setNames(c(COL_OBLIG, COL_SENT), SYSTEM_LABELS)
COL_PERIOD <- c(pre2020_partial = "#b8bec6", pre2020 = "#9aa3ad",
                covid = "#c9ced4", post2020 = "#2d3540")
LTY_PERIOD <- c(pre2020_partial = "solid", pre2020 = "solid",
                covid = "22", post2020 = "solid")
covid_rect <- national |>
  dplyr::filter(covid_season) |>
  dplyr::summarise(xmin = min(week_start), xmax = max(week_start) + 7)
sw_breaks <- c(1, 9, 14, 18, 23, 27, 36, 49)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        plot.title.position = "plot",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0)))
```

This report documents work package 4.2 of the Preliminary Study. It is generated
by `scripts/02_eda.R` (tables) and this file (report) from the datasets of WP 4.1;
every number below is computed, not typed.

# 1 Data

The analysis uses the national weekly series (`r nrow(national)` ISO weeks,
`r min(national$iso_week)` to `r max(national$iso_week)`,
`r dplyr::n_distinct(national$season)` seasons) and the stratified long table
(`r format(nrow(strata), big.mark = ",")` rows). Seasons run from W40 to W39.
Summary statistics across seasons exclude the incomplete season
`r paste(EDA_INCOMPLETE_SEASONS, collapse = ", ")` and
`r EDA_NO_SEASON` (no influenza circulation); both are still shown and flagged. Season
2025/26 is included: only the off-season weeks W38–W39 are missing.

```{r seasons-table}
national |>
  dplyr::group_by(season, period) |>
  dplyr::summarise(weeks = dplyr::n(),
                   complete = dplyr::first(complete_season),
                   in_summary = dplyr::first(in_summary),
                   test_season = dplyr::first(test_season),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Season", "Period", "Weeks", "Complete",
                             "In summary statistics", "Test season"))
```

# 2 Seasonal patterns

```{r fig-series, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(long, aes(week_start, value)) +
  geom_rect(data = covid_rect, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey92") +
  geom_line(aes(colour = system), linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ system, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = COL_SYSTEM, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "Weekly influenza activity in Switzerland, 2013-W01 to 2026-W37",
       subtitle = "Grey band: COVID-19 seasons 2020/21 and 2021/22")
```

**Overall pattern.** Both systems show one clear winter wave per season, with
low activity between seasons. The COVID-19 seasons interrupt the pattern
(2020/21 almost without influenza, 2021/22 with a late spring wave). From
2022/23 the mandatory reporting system runs at a clearly higher level,
while the Sentinella ILI rate does not rise to the same extent.

```{r fig-overlay, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(long, aes(season_week, value, group = season)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = period, linetype = period), linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ system, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = COL_PERIOD, name = "Period") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = LTY_PERIOD, name = "Period") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sw_breaks, labels = season_week_label(sw_breaks)) +
  labs(x = "Calendar week (season runs W40 to W39)", y = NULL,
       title = "All seasons overlaid on the season calendar")
```

```{r fig-typical, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(typical, aes(season_week, median, colour = period, fill = period)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75), colour = NA, alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ system, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = COL_PERIOD, name = "Period") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = COL_PERIOD, name = "Period") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sw_breaks, labels = season_week_label(sw_breaks)) +
  labs(x = "Calendar week (season runs W40 to W39)", y = NULL,
       title = "Typical season: median per week, pre-2020 vs post-2020",
       subtitle = "Band: interquartile range across seasons. COVID seasons, 2012/13 and lockdown weeks excluded")
```

```{r tab-periods}
periods |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(mean, median, p90, max), ~ round(.x, 2)),
                pct_zero = round(pct_zero, 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("System", "Period", "Seasons", "Weeks", "Mean", "Median",
                             "90th pct.", "Max", "% weeks = 0"),
               caption = "Weekly values per period")
```

*Interpretation (tbd): typical start, peak and end of the season;
level shift after 2020; how much seasons differ from each other.*

# 3 Peak timing and intensity

Peak week = week of maximum weekly value, peak intensity = that maximum
(Section 4.2), determined separately for both systems. If two weeks share the
maximum, the first is used. The peak lag is the oblig peak week minus the
Sentinella peak week (positive: Sentinella peaks earlier).

```{r tab-peaks}
peaks |>
  dplyr::transmute(season, period,
                   oblig_peak_week, oblig_peak = round(oblig_peak_value, 1),
                   sent_peak_week, sent_peak = round(sent_peak_value, 1),
                   peak_lag_weeks,
                   note = dplyr::case_when(!complete_season ~ "incomplete season",
                                           !in_summary ~ "no influenza season",
                                           test_season ~ "test season",
                                           TRUE ~ "")) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Season", "Period", "Peak week (oblig)", "Peak (cases/100k)",
                             "Peak week (Sentinella)", "Peak (ILI/1,000)", "Lag (weeks)", "Note"))
```

```{r fig-peak-week, fig.height = 5}
peaks |>
  dplyr::select(season, in_summary, oblig = oblig_peak_sw, sentinella = sent_peak_sw) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(oblig, sentinella), names_to = "system", values_to = "peak_sw") |>
  dplyr::mutate(system = factor(system, levels = c("oblig", "sentinella"), labels = SYSTEM_LABELS),
                season = factor(season, levels = rev(sort(unique(season))))) |>
  ggplot(aes(peak_sw, season, colour = system, shape = system)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = season), colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = COL_SYSTEM, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sw_breaks, labels = season_week_label(sw_breaks)) +
  labs(x = "Peak week", y = NULL, title = "Peak week per season") +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey95"))
```

```{r fig-peak-intensity, fig.height = 5}
peaks |>
  dplyr::select(season, in_summary, oblig = oblig_peak_value, sentinella = sent_peak_value) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(oblig, sentinella), names_to = "system", values_to = "peak") |>
  dplyr::mutate(system = factor(system, levels = c("oblig", "sentinella"), labels = SYSTEM_LABELS),
                season = factor(season, levels = rev(sort(unique(season))))) |>
  ggplot(aes(peak, season, fill = system, alpha = in_summary)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ system, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = COL_SYSTEM, guide = "none") +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1, `FALSE` = 0.35), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Peak intensity per season",
       subtitle = "Pale bars: 2012/13 (incomplete) and 2020/21 (no influenza season)")
```

```{r tab-peak-summary}
peak_sum |>
  dplyr::transmute(period, seasons,
                   oblig_week = sprintf("%s (SD %.1f, %s to %s)",
                                        season_week_label(round(oblig_peak_sw_mean)), oblig_peak_sw_sd,
                                        season_week_label(oblig_peak_sw_min), season_week_label(oblig_peak_sw_max)),
                   sent_week  = sprintf("%s (SD %.1f)", season_week_label(round(sent_peak_sw_mean)), sent_peak_sw_sd),
                   oblig_peak = round(oblig_peak_median, 1),
                   sent_peak  = round(sent_peak_median, 1),
                   lag = sprintf("%.1f (%d to %d)", lag_mean, lag_min, lag_max)) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Period", "Seasons", "Mean peak week oblig (SD in weeks, range)",
                             "Mean peak week Sentinella (SD)", "Median peak oblig", "Median peak Sentinella",
                             "Mean lag in weeks (range)"),
               caption = "Peak timing and intensity by period (seasons in summary statistics only)")
```

In `r sum(peaks$peak_lag_weeks > 0)` of `r nrow(peaks)` seasons the Sentinella
peak comes before the oblig peak, in `r sum(peaks$peak_lag_weeks == 0)` both
peak in the same week and in `r sum(peaks$peak_lag_weeks < 0)` the oblig peak
comes first. The largest gaps are in
`r paste(peaks$season[abs(peaks$peak_lag_weeks) >= 4], collapse = ", ")` (see
section 5).

*Interpretation (tbd): peak timing pre vs post 2020; higher oblig peaks
after 2020 partly reflect more testing (compare with Sentinella); relevance of
the peak lag for WP 4.3.*

# 4 Season onset and end

**Method.** Section 4.2 defines the onset as the first of two consecutive weeks
in which the Sentinella ILI rate exceeds the FOPH/BAG epidemic threshold of the
season, and the end as the last week above it. FOPH/BAG has not published an
ILI threshold since 2020/21, so – as agreed by the team – the threshold is
estimated with the Moving Epidemic Method (MEM; Vega et al. 2013, R package
`mem`), on the same scale as the FOPH/BAG threshold (ILI consultations per
100,000 inhabitants). For each season the threshold is estimated **only from
earlier seasons** (at most `r MEM_MAX_SEASONS`, at least `r MEM_MIN_SEASONS`;
complete seasons without COVID-19 seasons and without the lockdown weeks 2020),
so no information from the season itself is used. With fewer than
`r MEM_MIN_SEASONS` earlier seasons the estimate is unstable, therefore MEM
thresholds are available from `r min(mem_th$season[!is.na(mem_th$threshold_ili_per_100k)])`
onwards, which covers all test seasons.

**Validation against FOPH/BAG.** Estimated from all seven pre-2020 seasons, MEM
gives a threshold of `r round(validation$mem_retro_threshold[1], 1)` per 100,000,
within the range of the published FOPH/BAG thresholds
(`r min(bag_th$threshold_ili_per_100k, na.rm = TRUE)`–`r max(bag_th$threshold_ili_per_100k, na.rm = TRUE)`).
With this threshold, the onset rule reproduces the onset week reported by
FOPH/BAG in `r with(validation, sum(onset_mem_retro == onset_reported, na.rm = TRUE))` of
`r sum(!is.na(validation$onset_reported))` seasons; the prospective MEM
thresholds reproduce it in both seasons where they are available.

```{r tab-mem-validation}
validation |>
  dplyr::transmute(season, bag_threshold,
                   mem_threshold = round(mem_threshold, 1),
                   mem_retro = round(mem_retro_threshold, 1),
                   onset_reported, onset_bag, onset_mem, onset_mem_retro) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Season", "FOPH/BAG threshold", "MEM (prospective)",
                             "MEM (all pre-2020)", "Onset reported by FOPH/BAG",
                             "Onset with FOPH/BAG threshold", "Onset with MEM (prospective)",
                             "Onset with MEM (all pre-2020)"),
               caption = "Thresholds per 100,000 inhabitants and resulting onset weeks, pre-2020 seasons")
```

```{r tab-boundaries}
boundaries |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(threshold)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(season, threshold = round(threshold, 1), onset_week, end_week,
                   duration_weeks, sent_peak_week, oblig_peak_week,
                   share = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * oblig_share_in_window)) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Season", "MEM threshold", "Onset", "End", "Duration (weeks)",
                             "Peak Sentinella", "Peak oblig", "Oblig cases in window"),
               caption = "Season boundaries from Sentinella (MEM), applied to mandatory reporting")
```

```{r fig-boundaries, fig.height = 7}
win <- boundaries |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(threshold)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(national, season, onset_week = iso_week, on_sw = season_week),
                   by = c("season", "onset_week")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(national, season, end_week = iso_week, end_sw = season_week),
                   by = c("season", "end_week"))
national |>
  dplyr::filter(season %in% win$season) |>
  ggplot(aes(season_week, sentinella_ili_inc)) +
  geom_rect(data = win, aes(xmin = on_sw - 0.5, xmax = end_sw + 0.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey90") +
  geom_hline(data = win, aes(yintercept = threshold), linetype = "22", colour = "grey35") +
  geom_line(colour = COL_SENT, linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ season, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sw_breaks, labels = season_week_label(sw_breaks)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "ILI consultations per 100,000",
       title = "Season window per season (Sentinella, MEM threshold)",
       subtitle = "Dashed: MEM threshold from earlier seasons. Grey: onset to end")
```

*Interpretation (tbd): onset and duration pre vs post 2020; in 2020/21
the threshold is exceeded although almost no influenza circulated (ILI captures
SARS-CoV-2, see section 5); share of oblig cases inside the window; in-season
weeks for WP 4.5 in `output/eda/in_season_weeks.csv`.*
